item.description: I joined Microsoft Research in Redmond, WA as a Research Intern for Summer 2026.

item.title: 🎉 Passed my Ph.D. qualifier in CS — AI
item.description: I passed my Computer Science Ph.D. qualifying exam in the Artificial Intelligence area at Georgia Tech.

item.title: 🎉 CompanionCast accepted at the ACM CHI 2026 Workshop
item.description: — a framework for orchestrating multiple specialized AI agents as social collaborators in live shared experiences — was accepted at the ACM CHI 2026 Workshop on Human-Agent Collaboration. The paper will be published with the ACM AI Leadership Summit. The work builds on my Ph.D. research internship at Dolby Laboratories.

item.title: 📝 New preprint — MASCOT
item.description: We released , a multi-agent framework for multi-perspective socio-collaborative companions that improves persona consistency and reduces redundant, sycophantic dialogue. Read the .

item.title: 📄 PuffEM presented at CHASE 2025
item.description: , an e-cigarette sleeve that estimates user nicotine intake through multimodal sensing, was presented at the ACM/IEEE International Conference on Connected Health (CHASE 2025).

item.title: 🔬 Started a Ph.D. research internship at Dolby
item.description: I began a Ph.D. research internship at Dolby Laboratories, designing a multi-agent conversational AI framework with spatial audio to reimagine sports streaming through AI companions for social co-viewing.

item.title: 🏆 First place at the Graduate Poster Symposium
item.description: I received first place in the Junior Student category at the Georgia Tech College of Computing Graduate Poster Symposium for my research on multimodal sensing for health and well-being.

item.title: 🧑‍🏫 Started teaching Designing and Building User Interfaces
item.description: I began serving as a graduate teaching assistant for the online CS 8801 Designing and Building User Interfaces, where I designed the syllabus and curriculum and led biweekly seminars for the class.

item.title: 🎉 Presented work-in-progress at Northeast CHI
item.description: I presented my work-in-progress paper, From Puffs to Patterns: Ubiquitous Technology in Mapping E-Cigarette Consumption, at the Northeast CHI Symposium, sharing early results on multimodal sensing for understanding e-cigarette use.

item.title: ✅ Presented research to Georgia Tech President Cabrera
item.description: I had the chance to present our health-sensing research to Georgia Tech President Ángel Cabrera, discussing how multimodal sensing can support health and well-being.

item.title: 🧠 Started my Ph.D. at Georgia Tech
item.description: I started my Computer Science Ph.D. in the School of Interactive Computing at Georgia Tech, joining the Ka Moamoa Lab to work on human-AI interaction and multimodal sensing.

item.title: 📍 Presented MHCI capstone project with Meta
item.description: As part of my CMU MHCI capstone with Meta, our team presented Nova — an LLM-based assistant designed to improve knowledge sharing across data centers — at Meta’s Fremont office.

item.title: 👩🏼‍🏫 Volunteered at UbiComp 2022
item.description: I served as a selected student volunteer at UbiComp/ISWC 2022 in Atlanta, helping the program run smoothly while connecting with the ubiquitous computing research community.
